notes: Account: mid-market SaaS building a multichannel customer support agent used by 3rd-party merchants.
Primary ask: replace incumbent LLM API due to repeated latency regressions causing agent tool-call timeouts and user-visible stalls.
Started with Hosted API evaluation -> plan to move to Dedicated once SLA & throughput confirmed.
Customer quote (CTO): 'We can't have chat responses stall during third-party API calls — it's killing adoption.'
Cost sensitivity: moderate; willing to accept higher unit cost for guaranteed latency SLOs and predictable tail behavior.
Security: SOC2 required; will need SSO (SAML) and audit logging; some customers require data residency statements (US-only).
Internal stakeholders: Head of Product (trial owner), Infra Lead (owns POC), Security reviewer (legal).
Reference workload: 120 concurrent agents at peak, average session length 6 turns, heavy tool-calling to order/fulfillment APIs (external HTTP requests from within agent).
They provided an internal trace showing incumbent p95 spikes ~800ms and occasional 5s+ timeouts; want Redwood streaming to eliminate stalls and improve tool-calling reliability.

use_case_summary: Conversational agent integrated into merchant dashboards and mobile apps.
Agents perform multi-step tool calls: check order status -> call fulfillment API -> summarize results for merchant.
Must support streaming responses so UI shows partial answers while tool calls execute.
Strict tail-latency SLOs: p95 < 400ms for token streaming; agent end-to-end response (including tool calls) < 1.2s for normal flows.
Throughput target: sustained 1000 tokens/sec aggregate, peak 2500 tokens/sec during campaigns.
migration_reason: Observed latency regressions and inconsistent streaming from incumbent; repeated customer complaints about agent stalls and 3rd-party tool-call timeouts. Evaluating Redwood as replacement to regain predictable tail latency and streaming stability.
benchmark_findings: Redwood Hosted streaming median token latency: ~120ms vs incumbent ~310ms (synthetic workload simulating 10 concurrent agents).
Redwood p95 token latency: ~320ms vs incumbent p95 ~900ms; p99 shows similar advantage but requires longer run to stabilize.
End-to-end agent flows (including external tool HTTP calls): Redwood reduced observed UI stalls by ~55% in initial 48h run (fewer stream resets).
Streaming stability: Redwood had fewer reconnects/partial-chunk drops under noisy network emulation.
Tool-calling: function call handshake round-trip shorter with Redwood streaming hooks (less buffering), fewer timeouts observed in POC.
Cost: comparable per-token for hosted during POC; estimated ARR on Dedicated gives discount but requires commit to reach target price band.
notes_quick_hits: Decision criteria: latency SLOs (p95), streaming reliability, SLA for Dedicated, pricing band for 75-200k ARR.
They want a 72-hour continuous load run with true 3rd-party tool-call latencies simulated before buying Dedicated.
Legal wants DPA + data residency language confirmed before final PO.
